newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key Dec JGBs end easier as cash bond rises capped.
newsitem.headline: Key Dec JGBs end easier as cash bond rises capped.

text.p: Key December 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures closed easier on Monday as profit-taking emerged to inhibit cash bond rises.
"The market was quiet in the afternoon," said a long-term credit bank dealer. "The rally in the morning from last week's firmer tone was dampened when profit-taking emerged (in cash bonds)," he said.

The key December ended at 120.62, down 0.10 from Friday. The last-minute fall from around 120.70 was due to fresh selling by dealers after rolling over their shorts from the September which is to expire on Friday, traders said.

"Trade became directionless with the key contract caught in a range of around 120.60-120.70 in the afternoon," said a commercial bank dealer. "There are fears that U.S. interest rates may rise in the near future, and this curbed further buying in yen bonds. But no aggressive selling emerged either because even if U.S. rates are raised, Japan may not follow suit under the current economic situation," he said.
Earlier in the morning, the JGB market rallied, taking its cue from Japan's industrial output data which was announced after futures ended trading in Tokyo on Friday.
The key December contract hit a high of 120.90 soon after opening at 120.83. Its low was 120.58. It rebounded from there after digesting large-lot sales in long-term JGBs.

Growth of 4.1 percent in July industrial production was at the top end of market expectations, but weaker forecasts for August and September gave the market the impression that Japan's economic recovery was far from strong.

Another reason behind the early rise was an expectation that the Nikkei stock average would fall below 20,000 in line with plunges in U.S. stocks on Friday. But the index managed to stay above that level, and this cooled JGBs, traders said.

In the cash market, the yield of key 182nd 10-year JGBs fell to 2.925 percent in early trade, the lowest yield for a key 10-year bond since February 8. It stood at 2.940 percent at 0709 GMT, down 0.005 from Friday.
Traders said further buying is unlikely because few fresh factors are expected this week. But the key bond yield may be capped below 2.950 percent due to a lack of sellers.

"Those who wanted to take profits had already sold their holdings by now and others prefered keeping their assets (ahead of half-year book closings)," said the long-term credit bank dealer. -- Risa Maeda, Tokyo Treasury Desk (81-3-3432-8570)
